newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB to book one bln bfr excep gain.
newsitem.headline: UCB to book one bln bfr excep gain.

text.p: Belgian drugs and chemicals group UCB said on Friday the group would book a surplus of the order of one billion Belgian francs in 1997 following a share sale by one of its subsidiaries.
Societe Financiere UCB SA sold 8,429 shares, or 3.7 percent, in Financiere d'Obourg to holding company Financiere de Tubize.
UCB is Financiere de Tubize's main asset.
Holding company Financiere d'Obourg is also a major shareholder in UCB, holding over 30 percent.
Tubize is controlled by Belgium's Janssen family, founders of Belgian chemicals group Solvay, which it also controls via holding company Solvac.
Tubize and the Janssen family together own 68.28 percent of holding company Financiere d'Obourg, which holds around 37 percent of UCB.
Tubize chairman Daniel Janssen is Solvay's chief executive officer, deputy chairman of UCB and sits on Solvac's board. His brother, Eric Janssen also sits on the boards of UCB and Solvac.
UCB did not say when exactly or at what price it bought the Obourg shares. Financiere UCB had held the Obourg "for dozen of years," spokesman Alain Douxchamps told Reuters.
The transaction had been concluded on Friday. The selling prices had been "an average price over the last few months."
Obourg was down 700 francs at 184,300 at the Brussels bourse close on Friday.
At current market prices 8,429 shares are worth over 1.52 billion francs.
Obourg have been rising strongly. On May 24, 1995, the share was worth 31,150 francs. Since that day they have risen sixfold.

Douxchamps said that as a result of the deal Tubize's stake in Obourg now amounted to 63.5 percent. Obourg holds an exact 36.9 percent in UCB. Tubize's holding in UCB is only indirect, via Obourg, he added.
In 1996 Obourg and UCB Financiere were also at the heart of an exceptional gain, then 1.7 billion francs.
Banque du Luxembourg then sold 4.68 percent in UCB to UCB Financiere, which under company rules could not hold on to the shares and sold the stake via UCB on to holding company Financiere d'Obourg.
That deal raised Financiere d'Obourg's stake in UCB to over 30 percent. Under an agreement with Banque du Luxembourg it was done at the price at which the bank bought the shares in 1988.
The capital gain was free of tax because it involved a Luxembourg company and companies within the same group.
